expected_concepts: Cybernetic feedback loop between human mind and machine (cognitive + emotional + kinesthetic)
Excitatory homeostasis (Bryant + Davies, 2006) — choice of entertainment to achieve optimal arousal level
Mood-affecting qualities of games (mood as distinct from event-emotion — used by Calleja interchangeably with 'emotional states' rather than theorized separately)
Rhetorical strategies of affect (game design as imbued with affective rhetoric — recursive input/output extends non-ergodic rhetoric)
Escapism (Tuan 1998; Tolkien 1983; Evans 2001) — shift from one emotional state to a more favorable one with eventual return
Escape vs escapism distinction (escape = permanent one-way move; escapism = return trip)
Imagination as the faculty enabling escapism ('seeing what is not there')
Tolkien's 'secondary worlds' / 'inner consistency of reality' as habitable affective space
Aesthetic beauty of game environments as affective driver (landscape, lighting, sound, music)
Atmospherics — audiovisual contribution to mood (Inauro / Duskwood / Mirkwood passage; F.E.A.R. lighting + sound)
Negative affect as legitimate involvement (frustration, panic, fear, eeriness, shock, uncanny)
Affective transfer / cross-dimensional amplification (affect heightens spatial, ludic, shared involvement and vice versa)
AI 'director' as adaptive affect-modulation system (Left 4 Dead 2)
Verisimilitude vs media-pastiche affective registers (Red Orchestra vs Medal of Honor as paradigm case)
Suppressing fire as designed affect-generation mechanic (apprehension, urgency, near-panic)
Packaged experience — digitally mediated satisfaction of desires generated by movies, literature, fantasy
Designed vs precipitated affect (designer-intended emotional responses vs player-interpretation-generated responses)
Phase 0-flagged 'under-developed' status of the dimension itself (sparse theoretical scaffolding, only 2 substantive emotion-theory citations, no engagement with affect theory)

expected_interlocutors.role: Damasio, Ekman, Frijda, Plutchik, Nussbaum, Massumi, Sedgwick, Berlant, Barrett, Barsalou, Ahmed, Tomkins — ALL ABSENT from this chapter. Damasio (2000) IS cited elsewhere (Ch.10 Incorporation, p.167/169) but is NOT mobilized here despite explicit topic. This documents WHAT IS MISSING per Phase 2 special guidance.

expected_burke_pentad_candidate: Attitude — anticipatory projection per plan §4.1 (provenance: anticipatory-projection). Burke's pentadic Attitude term (the 'how' of action; the manner or mood with which Agency is exercised) is the cleanest pentad fit for Calleja's affective dimension: affect is the mood-tonality of involvement that modulates and is modulated by the other five dimensions (kinesthetic agency, spatial scene, shared agents, narrative act, ludic purpose). Burke himself extended the pentad to a hexad by adding Attitude precisely to capture this anticipatory-emotional dimension of motivation. Burke is wholly absent from Calleja's text and references (cite_check: 0 hits).
expected_uexkull_anchor_candidate: Merktöne / Wirktöne (perception-tones / effect-tones) — anticipatory projection per plan §4.1 (provenance: anticipatory-projection). STRONG BRIDGE per plan §1.4 flag. Uexküll's tone-doctrine holds that perceptual and effector signs are not affect-neutral data but carry intrinsic emotional-tonal coloration in the Umwelt (e.g., the tick perceives butyric acid not as molecule-data but as 'food-tone' / 'attack-tone'). Calleja's atmospherics passages — Duskwood's 'dark gloomy fantasy forest' tone, Night Elf Land's 'serene and pretty' tone, F.E.A.R.'s tense-and-dark atmosphere, suppressing-fire-induced apprehension-tone — are paradigmatically tone-coloration of perception-action loops. The Inauro passage on Mirkwood-evocation (line 4934-4939) is the cleanest single Uexküllian-tone exhibit in the volume. Calleja has zero Uexküll-vocabulary and zero biosemiotic citation.
expected_ontological_grounding_candidate: Aristotle pathē (the affective states catalogued in Rhetoric II) + Gross 2017 Uncomfortable Situations (situated-affect + Berlant cruel-optimism + Barrett constructed-emotion + Barsalou situated-conceptualization) — anticipatory projection per plan §1.4 (provenance: anticipatory-projection). Gross 2017 IS a confirmed corpus-index pipeline. The Gross frame would fill what Calleja's chapter manifestly lacks: a theory of how situated game-environments precipitate specific patterned affective responses; a theory of negative-affect-as-meaningful (rather than affect-as-arousal-tweaking); a theory of mood-vs-emotion distinction (which Calleja conflates); and a theory of cross-dimensional affective amplification (which Calleja observes but does not theorize). Aristotle's pathē supplies the classical-rhetorical anchor for treating affect as designed-rhetorical-effect (which Calleja explicitly calls 'rhetorical strategies of affect' at lines 4762-4764 and 5119 and 5156 — striking that he uses 'rhetorical' three times without invoking any rhetorical-theoretic tradition).
exegetical_anchors_for_layers: NONE — per Phase 0 cite-check. Calleja cites no Burke, no Uexküll, no Aristotle, no Merleau-Ponty, no Gibson-by-name, no Damasio in this chapter (though Damasio appears in Ch.10), no Ekman/Frijda/Plutchik/Tomkins, no Massumi/Sedgwick/Berlant/Ahmed/Barrett/Barsalou. The escapism theorists (Tuan, Tolkien, Evans) are cultural-imagination interlocutors, not affect theorists. All three dissertation augmentation layers (A=Aristotle/Heidegger, B=Burke, C=Uexküll) and the dissertation's Gross-2017 bridge are wholly anticipatory creative projection.

cross_pipeline_bridge_candidates.rationale: PROMINENT DISSERTATION-BRIDGE per plan §1.4. Calleja's chapter manifestly lacks (a) a theory of how situated environments precipitate specific affect (Berlant + Barsalou situated-conceptualization supplies this); (b) a theory of negative affect as more than arousal-tweak (Berlant cruel-optimism + Ngai 'ugly feelings' supply this); (c) a theory of mood/emotion distinction (Barrett constructed-emotion supplies this); (d) a theory of cross-dimensional affective amplification (Gross's situated-affect framing supplies this). The chapter's 'rhetorical strategies of affect' triple-invocation (lines 4762-4764, 5119, 5156) is a screaming anticipatory hook for affect-as-rhetoric grounding which Gross's frame would supply. Calleja does not cite Gibson, so the Gross-Calleja bridge cannot be anchored via shared-Gibson affordance theory (per Phase 0 cite-check). The bridge is singly-anchored anticipatory.

cross_pipeline_bridge_candidates.rationale: STRONG ANTICIPATORY BRIDGE per manifest cross-pipeline candidate list. Uexküll's Merktöne / Wirktöne (perception-tones / effect-tones) doctrine is the cleanest theoretical scaffolding for Calleja's atmospherics-as-affect treatment. The Inauro Duskwood-as-Mirkwood passage (lines 4934-4939) and the Aprile Night-Elf-Land passage (lines 5022-5027) read as paradigmatic Umwelt-with-tones case studies. The F.E.A.R. light-bulb-swaying / scampering-child sequence (lines 5077-5085) shows how Wirkmal-modulation (changing how objects behave) reshapes the Umwelt's affective tone. Calleja's text contains zero Uexküll-vocabulary; Gibson mediation hypothesis FALSIFIED.

cross_pipeline_bridge_candidates.pipeline: Burke (Grammar of Motives + Hawhee Moving Bodies)
cross_pipeline_bridge_candidates.rationale: Burke's Attitude pentad-term (the hexadic extension) is the cleanest pentad fit for the affective dimension. Burke is wholly absent from Calleja. Burke's own essays on attitude-as-incipient-act + the rhetoric of motives would supply theoretical grounding for Calleja's repeated 'rhetorical strategies of affect' formulation. Anticipatory.

BCAP's analyses of Stimmung (mood / attunement) as ontologically prior to event-emotion would supply the mood-vs-emotion distinction Calleja conflates. The escapism passages (especially Tuan-via-Calleja on imagination as 'mentally detaching ourselves temporarily from the present moment') touch ekstatic-temporal-attunement themes BCAP could ground. Anticipatory; Calleja's only Heidegger cite is QCT at p.21.

Calleja's extended Tuan-on-imagination passage (lines 4814-4831) — imagination as faculty of 'seeing what is not there' that retains past experiences + potential future actions alongside present-moment awareness — is a paradigmatic phantasia operation. Tolkien's 'secondary worlds' frame is structurally a phantasia-of-habitable-world. Anticipatory.

Aristotle's Rhetoric II catalogue of pathē supplies the classical-rhetorical scaffolding Calleja's 'rhetorical strategies of affect' phrasing implicitly invokes but does not theorize. Bowin AMT's aisthesis analyses bridge to the cognitive-emotional-kinesthetic feedback loop (line 4735). Anticipatory; zero Aristotle hits per Phase 0.

Affective dimension is a candidate operationalizable construct for the dissertation's empirical adaptation chapter. Calleja's relative under-development of this dimension makes it the PRIMARY dissertation-augmentation site: the Gross 2017 frame can substantively extend rather than merely re-describe Calleja's affective dimension. The chapter is anticipatory-bridge dense rather than exegetically dense.

SURPRISES AND FINDINGS: (1) Manifest interlocutor seed listed 'Bryant + Davies, Grodal' — VERIFIED present (only the latter pair cited by name in the chapter). The plan's anticipated emotion theorists (Damasio, Ekman, Frijda, Plutchik) are ALL ABSENT from this chapter; Damasio appears only in Ch.10 (p.167/169). Bernard Perron (game-affect, anticipated by the plan) is also ABSENT. (2) The chapter's PRIMARY conceptual interlocutor is Yi-Fu Tuan (1998) on escapism — a geographer of place + imagination, NOT an emotion theorist. The escapism-defense apparatus (Tuan + Tolkien + Evans) takes roughly the first 4-5 pages of the 12-page chapter. (3) Calleja uses 'rhetorical strategies of affect' THREE times (lines 4762-4764, 5119, 5156) without invoking any rhetorical-theoretic tradition — a striking anticipatory hook for Burke/Aristotle augmentation. (4) Calleja repeatedly observes cross-dimensional affective amplification (lines 3610, 4808-4810, 5072-5073, 5118-5123) but does not theorize the mechanism. (5) Calleja conflates mood and emotion throughout (e.g., 'moods and emotional states' as a paired-noun construction at line 4737-4738, line 4753-4757, line 4861) — the mood/emotion distinction is theoretically load-bearing in affect theory (Heidegger Stimmung; Massumi affect/emotion split; Barrett constructed-emotion) but is absent here. (6) Calleja's affective dimension is paradigmatically a SITUATED affect (game-environment precipitates response) — a structural alignment with Gross 2017 / Barsalou situated-conceptualization that the chapter itself does not articulate. (7) Game loci skew heavily toward FPS / action-horror (F.E.A.R., F.E.A.R. 2, Left 4 Dead 2, Medal of Honor, Red Orchestra) and toward WoW for aesthetic-affect — Silent Hill and Resident Evil (anticipated by the prompt as likely horror loci) are NOT cited; Half-Life 2 (anticipated by the prompt) is NOT cited. (9) Figure 8.1 captures a research-interview event in Teldrassil — methodologically notable, links the chapter to the underlying qualitative-interview substrate documented in Ch.3. (10) The chapter does not engage flow theory (Csikszentmihalyi) despite topical adjacency — confirms Phase 0 flag of Csikszentmihalyi absence as 'notable given Ch.8 Affective topic.'
